data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Manual (DM) provides processes and procedures in support of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy provided in Departmental Regulation (DR) 3410-001, Information Collection Request Activities: Collection of Information from the Public, dated January 26, 2022.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy
cross_references: Departmental Regulation (DR) 3410-001, Information Collection Request Activities: Collection of Information from the Public, dated January 26, 2022

policy_statements.source_text: This DM is effective immediately and remains in effect until it is superseded, or it expires.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their policies and procedures with this DM within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: This DM applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests (ICR).
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests (ICR)
conditions: that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests (ICR)

policy_statements.source_text: The following are the eight types of clearances that require an information collection (IC).
For new collections, 60 and 30 calendar day Federal Register Notices (FRN) are required to allow for public comment, along with IC instruments and supporting statements.
Revisions involve substantive changes to an approved IC.
Such revisions are generally a result of changes required by law or Mission Area, agency, or staff office action (e.g., program budget cuts).
Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) review and approval is required before revisions can be implemented.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA)
conditions: before revisions can be implemented

policy_statements.source_text: In this case, there are no changes to an approved IC’s information, such as the respondents, responses, or burden.
There can be reinstatement of an expired or discontinued IC.
It is acceptable to reuse the original OMB control number and IC instrument.

Verify with the Mission Area, agency, or staff office Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), Public Law (P.L.) 104-13, Clearance Officer or the OMB Desk Officer that the request will be accepted as a change versus a revision.
cross_references: Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), Public Law (P.L.) 104-13

policy_statements.source_text: Per OMB discretion (the OMB Desk Officer), a Mission Area, agency, or staff office may be allowed to publish a 30-day FRN instead of a 60-day FRN for a substantive change.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: Per OMB discretion (the OMB Desk Officer)
for a substantive change

policy_statements.source_text: These must be discussed and determined by the OMB Desk Officer.
If granted, an emergency extension cannot exceed 90 calendar days.
conditions: If granted

policy_statements.source_text: Some extenuating circumstances may be considered grounds for justifying an emergency approval.

These include circumstances that result or may result in public harm; that prevent the Mission Area, agency, or staff office from responding to an unanticipated event; or that cause the Mission Area, agency, or staff office to miss a statutory or court-ordered deadline.
Requests to discontinue IC is usually a result of a Mission Area, agency, or staff office decision that the IC is no longer needed.
The OMB response is within 5 business days.
FRNs are not required for each IC covered under the USDA, Mission Area’s, agency’s, or staff office’s fast track generic clearance.
conditions: for each IC covered under the USDA, Mission Area’s, agency’s, or staff office’s fast track generic clearance

policy_statements.source_text: Use for a common form must be obtained through approval from the Host agency sponsoring the form within or outside of USDA.
Prior to submitting the RCF, the program office must check with their Mission Area, agency, or staff office forms manager and the USDA Departmental Forms Management Officer (DFMO).
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office forms manager and the USDA Departmental Forms Management Officer (DFMO)
conditions: Prior to submitting the RCF

policy_statements.source_text: This process can be found in the Regulatory Information Service Center and Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs Consolidated Information System (ROCIS) document ROCIS How to Guide for Agency Users of the Information Collection Request (ICR) Module (“ROCIS Guide”).
cross_references: ROCIS How to Guide for Agency Users of the Information Collection Request (ICR) Module (“ROCIS Guide”)

policy_statements.source_text: The Mission Area, agency, or staff office along with the Agency Information Collection Officer (AICO) develops the information request and follows the instructions below.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office along with the Agency Information Collection Officer (AICO)

policy_statements.source_text: The Supporting Statement A is required for all ICRs.

It is comprised of 18 questions (see the ROCIS Guide, Section 26, Creating a Supporting Statement) that address the need for collecting the information from the public, how the information will be utilized by USDA, and how USDA will account for the burden on the public, whether by means of forms, surveys, or focus groups.
Note: The OMB Form 83-I, Paperwork Reduction Act Submission, is no longer used because the information contained on that form is now collected in ROCIS.
cross_references: OMB Form 83-I, Paperwork Reduction Act Submission

policy_statements.source_text: The Supporting Statement B is used for statistical methods only.

It is a document that consists of five questions (see the ROCIS Guide, Section 26, Creating a Supporting Statement) that allows the Mission Area, agency, or staff office to address statistical methods they plan to use within a survey.

Note: The National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) needs to review the completed package before it is forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Information Resource Management Center (IRMC), Information Management Division (IMD), Departmental Information Clearance Officers (DICO).
NASS only reviews the package if a Supporting Statement B is needed.
conditions: if a Supporting Statement B is needed

policy_statements.source_text: These instruments must contain the OMB control number, expiration date, public burden statement, and Privacy Act statement (see Appendices D, Public Burden Statement, and E, Privacy Act Statement, respectively).
Note: After the completion of Steps 1(a), 1(b), and 1(c) of the clearance process, forward the completed documents to the DICO and the USDA DFMO for review.
The Mission Area, agency, or staff office develops the 60-day FRN and follows the Mission Area, agency, or staff office process for its completion.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: The Mission Area, agency, or staff office receives and reviews comments from the public and provides responses as needed.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Note: Response to comments must be added to Question 8 in the Supporting Statement A (see the ROCIS Guide, Section 26, Creating a Supporting Statement), whether the comments are related to the collection or not.
conditions: whether the comments are related to the collection or not

policy_statements.source_text: They must also be added to the collection in ROCIS under the supplementary comments section.
The Mission Area, agency, or staff office consults with three individuals regarding burden estimates, time it takes to complete the forms and surveys, etc.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Upon completion of the consultations, the feedback is integrated into the Supporting Statement, forms, or surveys.
Once the Mission Area, agency, or staff office has finalized the information collection packet the DICO prepares and submits the 30-day notice to the Federal Register for comment.
conditions: Once the Mission Area, agency, or staff office has finalized the information collection packet

policy_statements.source_text: Note: For this notice, the AICO and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office must respond to comments if a response is warranted.
policy_statements.actor_name: AICO and the Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: if a response is warranted

policy_statements.source_text: These responses may be required by their Desk Officer to be added to the collection in ROCIS.
Upon publication of the 30-day FRN and the uploading of all required documents to ROCIS, the DICO submits the ICR to OMB.
conditions: Upon publication of the 30-day FRN and the uploading of all required documents to ROCIS

policy_statements.source_text: OMB reviews and engages with the Mission Area, agency, or staff office on any questions or comments prior to issuing a decision.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Note: During or after the 30-day comment period OMB may provide comments to the DICO and AICO for adjudication.
conditions: During or after the 30-day comment period

policy_statements.source_text: Once these comments have been adjudicated, the ICR will move to Step 8 below in the clearance process.
conditions: Once these comments have been adjudicated

policy_statements.source_text: This is a 3-year approval, unless otherwise directed by OMB within the notice of approval (NOA).
conditions: unless otherwise directed by OMB within the notice of approval (NOA)

policy_statements.source_text: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) – If an ICR collects PII, the responsible Mission Area, agency, or staff office must consult with their respective privacy office to ensure that the correct privacy information is incorporated into the collection and the necessary steps are taken to determine the following:
conditions: If an ICR collects PII

policy_statements.source_text: whether a privacy impact assessment (PIA) is required;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: whether a privacy threshold analysis (PTA) is required;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: and whether an existing system of records notice (SORN; see the USDA System of Records Notices web page) covers the information being collected.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Note: The Departmental Chief Privacy Officer (CPO) will only be consulted if the Mission Area, agency, or staff office does not have a Privacy Officer or if the Mission Area, agency, or staff office Privacy Officer seeks additional assistance from the CPO regarding PII in the collection.
conditions: if the Mission Area, agency, or staff office does not have a Privacy Officer or if the Mission Area, agency, or staff office Privacy Officer seeks additional assistance from the CPO regarding PII in the collection

policy_statements.source_text: Include the time needed to read instructions, gather records, complete a response, and submit the information to the Mission Area, agency, or staff office.
policy_statements.target: time needed to read instructions, gather records, complete a response, and submit the information to the Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must account for the time it takes for the respondents to complete the information.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: time it takes for the respondents to complete the information

policy_statements.source_text: To develop respondents’ cost, they must obtain current hourly wage information from the United States (U.S.) Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This can be found at:
Occupational Employment and Wages – May 2022; and
Employer Costs for Employee Compensation – December 2022.
cross_references: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation – December 2022

policy_statements.source_text: To request a Portable Document Format (PDF) copy of the burden conversion chart, contact the DICO at usda.pra@usda.gov.
To request a copy of the burden spreadsheet, contact the DICO at usda.pra@usda.gov.
OMB requires each Federal agency to submit an annual ICB estimating the hours of burden to be imposed on the public in the next fiscal year (FY) and verifying accomplishments in prior FYs.
Each FY, OMB determines the ICB format, reduction goals, and other required inputs.
policy_statements.target: ICB format, reduction goals, and other required inputs

policy_statements.source_text: It is the responsibility of the AICO and program leadership to provide the information to the IRMC Associate Chief Information Officer (ACIO) for the ICB.
All Mission Area-, agency-, or staff office-specific forms must be reviewed by the respective Mission Area, agency, or staff office forms manager.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office forms manager
policy_statements.target: All Mission Area-, agency-, or staff office-specific forms

policy_statements.source_text: All Agriculture Department (AD) forms must be received and reviewed by the USDA DFMO in the Departmental Forms Office within the Office of Budget and Program Analysis.
This must be done before OIRA submission, and again once OMB approval is received prior to finalization and publication of the form.
conditions: before OIRA submission, and again once OMB approval is received prior to finalization and publication of the form

policy_statements.source_text: These forms must include the OMB control number and expiration date in the upper right corner of the form, the OMB public burden statement, and the Privacy Act statement (if PII is being collected).
conditions: if PII is being collected

policy_statements.source_text: Standard forms are common forms.
In the event that a Mission Area, agency, or staff office must create an SF form, they must go through their forms manager and the USDA DFMO to obtain approval for use.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: In the event that a Mission Area, agency, or staff office must create an SF form

policy_statements.source_text: The Mission Area, agency, or staff office must submit an RCF in the ROCIS.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Optional forms are not always common forms.
In the event that a Mission Area, agency, or staff office must create an OF form as a common form, they must go through their forms manager and the USDA DFMO.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, or staff office
conditions: In the event that a Mission Area, agency, or staff office must create an OF form as a common form

policy_statements.source_text: Surveys and questionnaires must include the OMB control number and expiration date in the upper right corner of the form, the OMB public burden statement, and the Privacy Act statement (if PII is being collected).
conditions: if PII is being collected

policy_statements.source_text: The instruments category constitutes any other type of system or web-based instrument that the Mission Area, agency, or staff office will use to collect information from the public.
Instruments must include the OMB control number and expiration date in the upper right corner of the form, the OMB public burden statement, and the Privacy Act statement (if PII is being collected).
conditions: if PII is being collected

policy_statements.source_text: All forms being utilized for USDA ICs must be Plain Language and Section 508 compliant.
policy_statements.target: All forms being utilized for USDA ICs

policy_statements.source_text: The Secretary, USDA, will:
Comply with the requirements of the PRA and related policies as established by the OMB Director; and
policy_statements.target: requirements of the PRA and related policies

policy_statements.source_text: Delegate the responsibility for IC activities to the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO), serving as the Senior Agency Official (SAO) for IC within USDA.
The USDA CIO will:
Serve as the delegated SAO for IC activities and reports directly to the Secretary;
Serve as the focal point for all Departmentwide matters relating to ICRs, privacy, paperwork reduction, and burden reduction where applicable;
conditions: where applicable
policy_statements.resulting_status: focal point for all Departmentwide matters relating to ICRs, privacy, paperwork reduction, and burden reduction

policy_statements.source_text: Establish an office to manage USDA’s compliance with and implementation of the information policies and information resources management responsibilities, including the reduction of IC burdens on the public; and

Review and approve the Departmental ICR management policy, procedures, objectives, standards, and guidelines for the establishment and use of ICRs in accordance with governing statutes, regulations, policies, and procedures.
policy_statements.target: Departmental ICR management policy, procedures, objectives, standards, and guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: The OCIO ACIO for the IRMC will:
Designate one or two staff members to serve as the DICO; and
Submit the ICB to OMB in a timely manner to meet assigned due dates.
The OCIO-IRMC IMD Director will:
Review and approve the ICB for submission to the IRMC ACIO;

Review the Departmental ICR management policy, procedures, objectives, standards, and guidelines for the establishment and use of ICRs in accordance with governing statutes, regulations, policies, and procedures;
policy_statements.target: Departmental ICR management policy, procedures, objectives, standards, and guidelines

This Departmental Manual (DM) provides processes and procedures in support of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy provided in  Departmental Regulation (DR) 3410-001 , *Information Collection Request Activities: Collection of Information from the Public*, dated January 26, 2022.

This DM applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA that are involved with developing or processing information collection requests (ICR).
